questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
The transition of centrally planned economies to market economies was accompanied by a significant change in the composition of output. What was an immediate consequence of this transition?

options.A: a build-up of unsold stocks of goods
options.B: an increase in exports of goods
options.C: an increase in structural unemployment
options.D: decreasing prices of goods and services

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the production possibility curves of two economies, X and Y. capital X goods Y 0 65 100 200 consumer goods Which statement about the two economies is correct?

options.A: Both economies always have identical opportunity costs.
options.B: Both economies have the same future growth prospects.
options.C: The opportunity costs are constant in each economy.
options.D: The terms of trade for both countries will be one capital good for one consumer good.

questions.questionText: A production possibility curve shows labour-intensive farming output and capital-intensive manufacturing output. What would not cause a shift in this curve?

options.A: a reduction in sales tax on manufactured products
options.B: better training of workers in the manufacturing sector of the economy
options.C: improvements in the productivity of agricultural machinery
options.D: the reclamation of land to be used for both agriculture and manufacturing

questions.questionText: In calculating the short-run supply schedule for a firm, what is assumed to remain unchanged?

options.A: the number of consumers
options.B: the price of the good
options.C: the quantities of all factors
options.D: the state of technology

questions.questionText: There are two main types of coffee grown, arabica and robusta. The table gives details of the four largest coffee producers for 2013-2014. Production is measured in thousand 60 kilogram bags. coffee producer arabica coffee robusta coffee total output Brazil 39400 14400 53800 Vietnam 1175 27800 28975 Indonesia 1650 7850 9500 Colombia 11000 0 11000 What can be concluded from the table about production in the four countries?

options.A: Brazil has the highest level of specialisation.
options.B: Brazil produces more coffee than the other three named producers together.
options.C: Robusta coffee production is greater than arabica coffee production.
options.D: Vietnam has a comparative advantage in robusta and Colombia in arabica.

questions.questionText: A product with infinite elasticity of supply has sales of 1000 units a week at a price of $1 per unit. Price elasticity of demand is 1.5 over the relevant range. The government imposes a tax of 10%. What will be the government’s weekly tax revenue?
A government pays a subsidy to a country’s onion producers. With which price elasticity of demand (PED) will this action be most effective in reducing the price of onions?

options.A: PED equals 0.
options.B: PED is greater than 0 but less than 1.
options.C: PED equals 1.
options.D: PED is greater than 1 but less than infinity.

questions.questionText: Which statement best describes a transfer payment?

options.A: It is a loan from the government to help firms.
options.B: It is a payment to individuals not linked to economic activity.
options.C: It is the redistribution of income from government to individuals for work done.
options.D: It is the redistribution of income from households to firms for goods purchased.

questions.questionText: On 1 May 2012 President Morales of Bolivia announced the nationalisation of Transportadora de Electricidad (TDE), a subsidiary of a Spanish company that owned and ran approximately three-quarters of Bolivia’s power grid. What can be concluded from this?

options.A: Bolivian employees of TDE will own 100% of its shares.
options.B: Only Bolivian nationals will be allowed to work at TDE.
options.C: TDE company shares will be sold to a Bolivian company.
options.D: The Bolivian government will take over ownership of TDE.

questions.questionText: An economy faces rising raw material costs and a fall in business confidence. How will the economy’s real GDP and the price level be affected? real GDP price level

options.A: it may rise or fall it will rise
options.B: it will fall it may rise or fall
options.C: it will fall it will fall
options.D: it will rise it may rise or fall

questions.questionText: The UK inflation rate as measured by the Consumer Price Index was 5.2% in September 2011. In June 2014 the UK inflation rate as measured by the Consumer Price Index was 1.6%. What can definitely be concluded about the period September 2011 to June 2014?

options.A: Fixed income earners had increased purchasing power.
options.B: Prices were falling.
options.C: The rate of price increases was slowing.
options.D: The real rate of interest became positive.

questions.questionText: If a country has a surplus in its balance of payments then its money supply is likely to

options.A: fall because more of its goods were purchased by foreign consumers than by consumers at home.
options.B: increase because the foreign currency received for exports will be exchanged for domestic currency.
options.C: remain constant because the surplus is automatically offset by a loan for the deficit countries.
options.D: remain unchanged because its exports are bought with foreign currency.

questions.questionText: What is the main argument a government of a small country might use in times of a worsening worldwide recession to justify an increase in import tariffs and other trade protectionist policies?

options.A: to protect the country from a rise in domestic unemployment
options.B: to protect the country’s terms of trade
options.C: to protect the domestic economy from increasing prices
options.D: to protect the domestic economy from the import of poor quality goods

questions.questionText: What would be classified as a supply-side policy measure?

options.A: a law to alter the power of trade unions
options.B: a reduction in the government’s fiscal deficit
options.C: an open market sale of securities
options.D: the imposition of a tariff on imported goods

options.A: a cut in income tax rates
options.B: a depreciation of the exchange rate
options.C: the removal of government subsidies to producers
options.D: the removal of limits on bank lending
